questions.text: What is an array and what are its key characteristics?

rubric.definition: Should mention: collection of elements, indexed access, contiguous memory, homogeneous data type
rubric.reasoning: Should explain why arrays are efficient for random access
rubric.application: Should give an example use case

questions.text: Explain the time complexity of accessing, inserting, and deleting elements in an array.

rubric.definition: Should state O(1) for access, O(n) for insert/delete at beginning/middle
rubric.reasoning: Should explain why these complexities occur (shifting elements)
rubric.application: Should discuss when to use arrays vs other data structures

questions.text: Explain how bubble sort works and its time complexity.

rubric.definition: Should describe pairwise comparisons and swapping
rubric.reasoning: Should explain why it's O(n²) in worst/average case
rubric.application: Should mention when bubble sort might be appropriate

questions.text: Compare and contrast merge sort and quick sort.

rubric.definition: Should define both algorithms (divide and conquer)
rubric.application: Should discuss use cases for each

questions.text: Explain the binary search algorithm and its prerequisites.

rubric.definition: Should describe halving search space, sorted array requirement
rubric.reasoning: Should explain O(log n) time complexity
rubric.application: Should give an example problem solved by binary search

questions.text: Write pseudocode for binary search and explain each step.

rubric.definition: Should include left/right pointers, midpoint calculation
rubric.application: Should discuss edge cases (empty array, element not found)

questions.text: What is recursion and what are its base case and recursive case?

rubric.definition: Should define recursion as self-referential function calls
rubric.reasoning: Should explain need for base case to prevent infinite recursion

questions.text: Explain the call stack in recursion and potential issues.

rubric.definition: Should describe stack frames and memory usage
rubric.reasoning: Should explain stack overflow risk with deep recursion
rubric.application: Should discuss when to use recursion vs iteration

questions.text: What is backtracking and how does it differ from brute force?

rubric.definition: Should define backtracking as incremental solution building with pruning
rubric.reasoning: Should explain how it avoids exploring invalid paths

questions.text: Explain the general template for backtracking algorithms.

rubric.reasoning: Should explain recursion tree and pruning conditions
